resources.string: Example lactating lobule and enlarged alveolus
Lobule
A lobule contains groups of small milk-producing sacs called alveoli. The right-hand illustration enlarges one sac to show its cell layers.
Branching duct
Small ducts join larger branches that carry milk. This schematic shows one portion of a branching network, not the total number of ducts.
Deep calf from behind, superficial muscle removed
Soleal arch
An upper fibrous arch spans between the tibial and fibular attachments of the soleus.
Soleus fibers
The soleus lies under the gastrocnemius. Its fibers angle into broad tendinous sheets rather than running straight to the heel.
Tendinous sheet
This example shows a flattened tendinous sheet that collects muscle force and connects with the Achilles tendon below.
Calcaneus
The Achilles tendon attaches here at the heel, transferring calf muscle force to the foot.
Clavicle from above with its two joints
Sternal end
The thicker, medial end meets the top of the sternum at the sternoclavicular joint.
Curved shaft
The S-shaped shaft acts as a strut, holding the shoulder away from the chest wall.
Acromial end
The flatter, lateral end meets the acromion of the scapula. Both joints contribute motion when the arm rises.
The fibula alongside the tibia and ankle
Fibular head
This upper end meets the upper tibia just below the knee. It does not form a joint with the femur.
Fibular shaft
The slender bone runs along the outside of the lower leg and provides attachment for muscles.
Interosseous membrane
A fibrous sheet connects the shafts of the tibia and fibula.
Lateral malleolus
The lower end of the fibula forms the bony point on the outside of the ankle and borders the talus.
